equation_checks.finding: The route uses a_i=⟨ψ_i|φ_r⟩; the inherited Born score uses its conjugate, with the same squared modulus. C preserves the denominator and utilities and sends H to H*, so U_C(t)=U(-t)*. Both routed readouts therefore equal their original readouts at −t. These are exact-arithmetic identities, not bitwise guarantees.
For ȧ=−iHa, the derivative of |a_i|² is +2 Im[(Ha)_i a_i*]. Hermiticity makes the pair currents antisymmetric, yielding the stated (u_ri−u_rj) sign and i[H,V] convention.

The source Gram entry is ⟨ψ_i|ψ_j⟩, giving the oriented product in (2), not its conjugate. All ray phases cancel. Subtracting the two separately norm-scaled generators gives (3) on nonzero graphs; for a singleton both currents vanish without forming scale ratios.

Diagonal initial density and readout force zero slope. At −t the transition-probability matrix is the transpose of its value at t, not necessarily the same matrix. Complex cycle phases can thus produce a cubic odd term; they do not guarantee one.

The εI contributions cancel on valid tokens. Centering V gives norm Δ/2, so three commutators bound |d'''| by 4Δ‖σ‖₁. The odd Taylor remainder has factor |t|³/6, giving Δ‖σ‖₁/96 at t=1/4 and the strict slope threshold Δ‖σ‖₁/24. This certifies the odd contrast, not d(1/4) itself.

Both routes start at native logits, so the coherent CE slope is (p−onehot(y))·j and the dephased slope is zero. At fixed input and label, C preserves p and reverses j. A C-invariant head law therefore cancels integrable signed odd responses in expectation; native loss invariance alone does not establish that law.
